content: The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) is an Australian government agency responsible for collecting and publishing statistical information about Australia and its population. The agency conducts the Australian Census of Population and Housing every five years, as mandated by the Census and Statistics Act of 1905, Section 8. The most recent census was conducted on August 8, 2006, and the results were made available on the ABS website starting June 27, 2007. Since 1978, the ABS has been conducting surveys to gather data on research and development (R&D) expenditures and human resources dedicated to R&D in Australia. These surveys provide insights into the nature and distribution of R&D activities, which are used by government policy analysts, advisors, businesses, and economists. The ABS conducts four types of R&D surveys: the Business R&D survey (annually), the Higher Education R&D survey (biennially), the General Government R&D survey (biennially), and the Private Non-Profit Sector R&D survey (biennially). The ABS reports R&D data using the Australian Standard Research Classification (ASRC). The first ASRC was introduced in 1993 and was used until 1998. It included three classification schemes: Type of Activity (TOA), Field of Research (FOR), and Socio-Economic Objective (SEO). In 1998, a revised ASRC was released, replacing FOR with Research Field, Course, and Discipline (RFCD) and updating the SEO classification. This revised classification was implemented during the 2000 collection period, with data submissions due by August 31, 2001. The TOA classification categorizes R&D activities based on the type of research effort, such as pure basic research, strategic basic research, applied research, and experimental development. The RFCD classification allows for categorization of both R&D activities and other activities within the higher education sector. Before 1998, this information was collected using the FOR classification. The RFCD classification was expanded to include courses, units of study, and teaching activities in higher education, covering recognized academic disciplines, major research fields, and emerging areas of study. The SEO classification categorizes R&D based on its intended purpose, as perceived by the researcher. It includes distinct economic, social, technological, or scientific domains to identify the primary goal of the R&D. The SEO classification incorporates attributes related to processes, products, health, education, and other social and environmental aspects of interest. The ABS publishes an annual reference work called the Year Book Australia, which provides a comprehensive and detailed statistical overview of various aspects of Australia's economy and social conditions. It also includes descriptive content on Australia's geography, climate, government, international relations, defense, education, and health and welfare systems. Since 1975, the head of the ABS has been referred to as the Australian Statistician. Previously, this position was known as the Commonwealth Statistician. A complete list of officeholders is available under the title Australian Statistician. The current Australian Statistician, as of March 2007, is Brian Pink.
